membrane_recover — DRIVE tacsim op

• Data kinds: rgb × matrix × scalar → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.membrane_recover(rgb, lights, pitch: 'float', ambient: 'float' = 0.0, albedo: 'float' = 1.0) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import tacsim; tacsim.membrane_recover(rgb, lights, pitch: 'float', ambient: 'float' = 0.0, albedo: 'float' = 1.0) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("membrane_recover"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Visuotactile RGB (H, W, 3) → treats the 3 channels as images under 3 lights and obtains normals with photometric.photometric_stereo (lit_only) → height with photometric.integrate_normals (Frankot-Chellappa) (pixel units × pitch = m).

ambient and albedo are calibration values: albedo·ambient is subtracted from the image before solving (Woodham's linear model has no ambient term of the synthetic albedo·(N·L + ambient), so without the subtraction the normals lean towards z and the tilt comes out systematically smaller by ambient/sin(elevation) ≈ 3.7 % (0.03/0.82) —— this corresponds to reference-frame calibration on real hardware. It was the cause of δ being 3.5 % low in the prototype).

Returns: normals (H, W, 3), albedo (H, W), height (H, W) [m, relative value with mean 0], pitch. Raises ValueError: rgb is not (H, W, 3), pitch ≤ 0, ambient < 0. Empty input (rgb with 0 elements) raises ValueError.
